citation: UniProt Q96Q04 (seq v2, 1460 aa) + Pfam PF07714 domain 133-411; this work, motif-anchored scorecard
claim_tested: LMTK3 kinase domain retains the five catalytic elements
key_finding: Gly-rich loop G140-G145 (GSGWFG); beta3 Lys K164; alphaC Glu E181; catalytic loop H264-S265-D266-L267-A268-L269-R270-N271 with catalytic Asp D266 (= sole UniProt ACT_SITE) and Mg2+ Asn N271; Mg2+ motif D284-Y285-G286; APE A311-P312-E313. 5/5 elements present.
context: human Q96Q04, in silico; pseudokinase controls ERBB3/STRADA/KSR1 scored as deficient in the same run
limitation: sequence presence does not prove activity

citation: UniProt proteome scan, 125 non-fragment vertebrate LMTK3 orthologs (125 species); this work
claim_tested: Catalytic residues are conserved across vertebrate orthologs
key_finding: Catalytic Asp and catalytic-loop +7 Asn in 125/125 (100%). Catalytic loop HSDLALRN in 122/125, HSDMALRN in 3/125. DYG in 125/125.
limitation: database redundancy; most entries are automatic annotations from genome projects

citation: This work, reviewed human kinome scan (474 Pfam-kinase entries, 430 domains parsed)
claim_tested: Are the LMTK3 deviations HSD and DYG rare or tolerated variants?
key_finding: HRD+1 Ser in 4/430 (0.93%): AATK, LMTK2, LMTK3, TTK. DYG in 10/430 (2.33%). The exact 8mer HSDLALRN occurs in exactly 3 kinases, the entire LMTK family. DYG and non-RD co-occur more than chance (Fisher OR=5.4, p=0.014).
limitation: 44/474 entries had no parseable Pfam kinase domain and were excluded

citation: Hanks & Quinn specificity rules applied to Q96Q04; this work
claim_tested: Specificity class is determinable from catalytic-loop and activation-segment residues
key_finding: LMTK3 scores 6/8 to HRDLAARN (TK) vs 4/8 to HRDLKPEN (STK); HRD+4 = Ala268 (TK diagnostic); P+1 loop L307-R308-W309-A310-A311-P312-E313 carries the TK-diagnostic Trp309. The signature is TK-type. The Ala at catalytic-loop +4 is shared by 74/430 human kinases, so it marks the TK branch of the kinome.
limitation: the rule predicts branch membership, and the branch assignment conflicts with the measured transferase activity (E5, E6)

claim_tested: Does the TK-type motif predict tyrosine transferase activity in the LMTK family?
key_finding: LMTK2/KPI-2, which carries the identical HSDLALRN and DYG motifs as LMTK3, phosphorylates Ser/Thr and shows no tyrosine kinase activity.
limitation: paralog inference: the assay was on LMTK2, not LMTK3

citation: PMID 21602804 (Giamas et al., LMTK3 and ESR1)
claim_tested: Is LMTK3 itself catalytically active, and on which residues?
key_finding: Sole experimental source behind GO:0106310 (EXP) and behind the UniProt CATALYTIC ACTIVITY statements RHEA:17989 (Ser) and RHEA:46608 (Thr), EC 2.7.11.1, both ECO:0000269. Also the sole source of the GO:0005515 IPI with ESR1 (P03372).
limitation: a single publication carries the entire experimental GO base for this gene; no independent replication is annotated

citation: PDB 6SEQ chain A; AlphaFold AF-Q96Q04-F1; Modi & Dunbrack (2019) PNAS spatial criteria; this work
claim_tested: Does an LMTK3 coordinate set show a catalytically productive active site?
key_finding: 6SEQ: D1=12.12 A, D2=9.45 A -> DFG-out; K164-E181 ion pair 7.21 A (broken). AlphaFold: D1=11.46, D2=9.35 -> DFG-out; ion pair 2.74 A (formed). Active references: PKA 1ATP 6.23/14.59 (3.63 A), SRC 1Y57 6.58/14.69 (2.82), INSR 1IR3 6.13/14.37 (4.39). No LMTK3 model is simultaneously DFG-in and alphaC-in.
context: human; one crystal form plus one prediction
limitation: DYG tyrosine is bulkier than Phe, so the Dunbrack thresholds calibrated on DFG may misclassify DYG kinases; n=1 crystal structure

claim_tested: Internal consistency of the reference annotation
key_finding: SIMILARITY says 'Tyr protein kinase family' (ECO:0000255, PRU00159) while CATALYTIC ACTIVITY gives RHEA:17989/RHEA:46608 and EC 2.7.11.1 (ECO:0000269 PubMed:21602804). The sequence-model call and the experimental call disagree on class.

citation: PMID 42645201 (LMTK3 activating mutation) mapped onto Q96Q04 by isoform offset; this work
claim_tested: Does a point mutation modulate LMTK3 catalytic output, and where does it sit?
key_finding: Reported L313R is Q96Q04 L287R, which is DYG+3 in the activation segment. Reported Ser1258 is Q96Q04 S1232; region 1181-1486 is Q96Q04 1155-1460. Offsets: XP_011524713 (1486 aa) = +26, XP_011524714 (1475 aa) = +15, PDB 6SEQ construct = +29.
limitation: offsets derived by exact-substring containment; curators should re-verify against the paper's stated accession
